
`simulab` separates a simulation into three ideas: define the data-generating
process, generate primary observations, and retrieve known truth as tidy tables.

## A declarative study

```{r}
library(simulab)

specification <- define_variables(
  define_variable("baseline", 0, 1, "normal"),
  define_variable("treatment", 0.5, distribution = "binary"),
  define_variable(
    "outcome",
    "0.5 * baseline + treatment",
    1,
    "normal"
  )
)

study <- simulate_study(200, specification, seed = 42)
head(study)
components(study)
```

## Specialized data with ground truth

```{r}
growth <- simulate_growth(
  n = 100,
  times = 0:4,
  intercept = 10,
  slope = 0.5,
  seed = 42
)

head(growth)
as.data.frame(growth, what = "parameters")
```

## Repeated scenarios

```{r}
scenarios <- scenario_grid(
  mean_b = c(0, 0.5),
  replications = 3
)

batch <- simulate_scenarios(
  scenarios,
  simulator = "ttest",
  n_a = 20,
  n_b = 20,
  mean_a = 0,
  seed = 100
)

head(batch)
```
